nodes.title: Environmental variability and pressure-state relationships
nodes.research_question: How do climate and oceanographic variability, natural forcing, fishing pressure, and their interactions alter productivity and the state of pelagic populations?
nodes.why_it_matters: Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems are highly variable, so separating environmental forcing from fishing effects is essential for detecting pressure-state relationships, thresholds, and regime changes.

nodes.title: Fisheries dynamics and adaptive management
nodes.research_question: How do pelagic fisheries reorganize through seasons, environmental variability, fleet behaviour, and management interventions, and how can those dynamics inform adaptive decisions?
nodes.why_it_matters: Fast changes in resource availability and fishing operations require diagnostics that separate ecological availability, biological risk, fishing pressure, and fleet response.

nodes.title: Reproductive biology, growth and condition
nodes.research_question: How do reproduction, growth, and individual condition vary through time, and how do these life-history processes contribute to changes in pelagic population state?
nodes.why_it_matters: Maturity, spawning, growth, and condition can respond before biomass does, providing complementary information on population performance and resilience.

nodes.title: Scientific computing and research software
nodes.research_question: How can statistical methods, reproducible workflows, and research software make complex marine and fisheries analyses more transparent, reusable, and auditable?
nodes.why_it_matters: Heterogeneous marine data and complex models create hidden analytical variation; reusable software and reproducible workflows improve validation, transferability, and scientific efficiency.

nodes.title: Spatial ecology, species distribution and biodiversity
nodes.research_question: How do pelagic species, associated fauna, and non-target interactions vary across space and time, and which environmental processes shape habitat suitability and species distributions?
nodes.why_it_matters: Spatially explicit information from niche models, species distribution models, biodiversity observations, and bycatch patterns is needed to interpret ecosystem change and support spatial fisheries management.

nodes.title: Stock assessment and population dynamics
nodes.research_question: How do population processes, productivity, and model assumptions shape inference about the state and dynamics of exploited pelagic populations?
nodes.why_it_matters: Reliable assessment requires integrating biomass with recruitment, mortality, selectivity, and productivity while accounting for structural uncertainty in the models used for fisheries advice.
